bull.b: Sustained NII growth and a rising NIM provide a durable core earnings driver for a retail-commercial bank. With strong deposit and loan growth noted, steady interest-spread income supports predictable cash generation across rate cycles, improving baseline profitability even if markets soften.

Broad-based fee growth across investment banking, wealth and markets reduces reliance on cycles in lending. High performance in trading and advisory bolsters non-interest revenue durability, helping stabilize earnings through market volatility and supporting long-term franchise value beyond pure net interest margins.

Ample capital and a large, stable deposit base underpin funding resilience and regulatory cushion. The capacity to return capital while maintaining CET1 near policy targets signals durable franchise economics and management confidence, supporting long-term flexibility for lending, investment and shareholder distributions.

bear.b: A meaningful increase in leverage heightens sensitivity to funding stresses and interest-rate shifts. Higher debt/equity amplifies downside in a credit or liquidity shock, reducing financial flexibility and increasing the risk that cyclical downturns or market dislocations could more quickly pressure capital and earnings.

Elevated NPLs and sizeable criticized commercial exposures create potential for reserve build and earnings volatility if credit conditions worsen. Even isolated corporate losses can become broader loss trends in a downturn, threatening loan profitability and capital if provisions must rise materially.

While recent operating cash improved, historical volatility and intermittent negative free cash flow reduce predictability of internal funding and buybacks. Choppy top-line trends imply earnings reliance on transient market cycles, making multi-period planning and consistent capital deployment more challenging.
